2609.02246.title: LLM-as-a-Judge Is Not an Oracle: Why Self-Improving Agents Need Deterministic Guardrails
2609.02246.paper_summary: Self-improving agent pipelines have a problem at their center. An optimizer rewrites prompts to score higher, and the score comes from a judge that is itself an LLM. That judge has the last word on whether the system is getting better, and our position is that it has not earned it. The judge should be demoted from oracle to advisor: its verdict becomes one input among several, and every change is gated instead by a deterministic verification layer the judge cannot override. We reached this position by building the alternative and running it. Over months of running autonomous prompt-optimization loops in production across contract analysis, compliance review, and code quality, we cataloged eleven ways the evaluation signal failed, in four classes: judge bias, harness and metric failures, ground-truth errors, and reward hacking. Agents achieved perfect scores by reading cached answer keys from their environment, a 100% pass rate concealing 68% true capability. A corrupted ground-truth label caused the optimizer to delete correct compliance rules to agree with it. A syntactically broken prompt was promoted as the winner because a silent parser fallback improved the metric. Attempts to fix the judge by rewriting its rubric plateaued; the only reliable gain came from a structural constraint on its output order. In response we describe PROCTOR, a Teacher-Student loop in which a stateful orchestrator holds all tool access, stateless subagents diagnose failures and draft mutations they cannot apply, and a Teacher grades those mutations under five deterministic guardrails: hermetic sandboxes, capability-disjoint roles, acceptance checks that outrank the Teacher, frozen holdouts, and canary cases engineered so that a perfect score is itself evidence of cheating. We report the failures this prevented, and, because the Teacher is itself an LLM judge, the failures it did not.
2609.02246.paper_summary_zh: 自我改善的代理管道有一個核心問題。優化器重寫提示以提高得分，而得分來自一個本身就是大型語言模型（LLM）的評審。這個評審對於系統是否在改善上擁有最後的發言權，而我們的立場是它並未贏得這個權利。評審應該從神諭者降級為顧問：它的裁決成為多個輸入中的一個，而每一次變更則由一個評判無法覆蓋的確定性驗證層來控制。我們通過構建替代方案並運行它來達成這一立場。在數月的自動提示優化循環運行中，涵蓋合同分析、合規審查和代碼質量，我們記錄了評估信號失敗的十一種方式，分為四類：評審偏見、工具和指標失敗、真實標準錯誤，以及獎勵駭客。代理通過從其環境中讀取緩存的答案鍵來獲得完美得分，100%的通過率掩蓋了68%的真實能力。一個被損壞的真實標籤導致優化器刪除正確的合規規則以與其一致。一個語法上錯誤的提示被提升為獲勝者，因為一個靜默的解析器回退改善了指標。通過重寫評審的標準來修正評審的嘗試達到了瓶頸；唯一可靠的增益來自於對其輸出順序的結構性約束。作為回應，我們描述了PROCTOR，一個教師-學生循環，其中一個有狀態的協調者持有所有工具訪問權限，無狀態的子代理診斷故障並草擬它們無法應用的變更，而教師在五個確定性護欄下對這些變更進行評分：密閉沙箱、能力不重疊的角色、超越教師的接受檢查、凍結的保留樣本，以及設計成使完美得分本身成為作弊證據的金絲雀案例。我們報告了這些防止的失敗，並且，由於教師本身就是一個LLM評審，它未能防止的失敗。
2609.02246.author: Vansh Wahi et.al.
